title: a, d, g and q are all a circle and a line: free alphabet chart
text:
On a handwriting alphabet chart, a, d, g and q are each a circle and a straight line. They are the shapes a child is taught to write, not the "a" and "g" with a hook over the top that you see in a printed book.

So how do you tell g from q? The tail. g's tail curls to the left, q's curls to the right.

Also on the chart: b and p are a line first, then a bump on its right side, so they mirror d and q. Lowercase l and the number 1 are both one straight line, so they look the same.

The chart is one free printable page, 8.5×11: Aa to Zz in pairs on four-line handwriting guides, then 0 to 9 along the bottom. Schools use different handwriting models, so compare it with the one your child's school uses before you pin it up.

To practise each letter, the free A to Z letter tracing worksheets give every letter its own page: numbered start dots, stroke arrows, then rows to trace.

title: KDP spine text: 79 pages or 80? KDP says both
text:
When can a KDP paperback have text on its spine? KDP's own help pages give two answers.

"To include spine text, your book must have at least 79 pages." (Create a Paperback Cover)
"We only print spine text on books with more than 79 pages." (the same page)
"The minimum page count required to include text on the spine is 80 pages." (Cover Creator)

In October 2026 a book KDP counted at 79 pages had its spine text refused on the KDP Community forum. So plan on 80, and count the pages in the PDF file, not the number on the last page.

At 80 pages on 6 x 9 white paper the spine is 0.180", and only 0.055" of it is left for text once you keep 0.0625" inside each fold. That is about 3.5 pt of bold type. Cream paper: 0.200" and 0.075".

title: Writing 0 to 9, only 4 and 5 lift the pencil
text:
Writing 0 to 9, only two numbers lift the pencil: 4 and 5. That's 12 strokes for all ten digits, counted from the shapes on the free worksheets.

4: start at the top left, down to the middle and across. Lift. Then a long line down on the right.
5: start at the top left, down to the middle and round. Lift. Then the top line, last.

The other eight are one stroke each. 0 goes round to the left, all the way back to the top. 8 is an S to the bottom, then a line back up to the start.

The start dots and arrows follow a published school number formation chart. Schools use different models, so check them against the one your child's school uses.

The free number tracing worksheets are ten printable pages, 8.5×11, one for each digit: the number large with numbered start dots and stroke arrows, rows to trace, then room to write it alone.

title: Free cursive practice sheets for adults: 12 rows a page, A to Z
text:
Free cursive practice sheets sized for adults: 0.45" lines, 12 rows to a page. The free Trace Press cursive sheets for children have 5 rows a page on bigger lines. Both counts are from the PDFs.

Each sheet is one letter, A to Z, 26 sheets in one PDF, 8.5×11:
- the capital and lowercase letter once in solid cursive
- rows of them in light grey to write over
- rows that start with one grey letter and leave the rest of the line to you

Every row has four-line guides: a top line, a dashed midline, a solid baseline, and a dotted line for tails. The 0.45" is the height from the top line to the baseline.

The letters are the Playwrite US Trad font, a traditional American cursive, free under the SIL Open Font License. Other cursive models shape some capitals differently.

title: 12 lowercase letters, 3 first moves: a d g q, b h k l, i m n r
text:
12 of the 26 lowercase letters start with one of just three first moves, counted from the letter shapes in the Trace Press worksheets.

1. A circle, counterclockwise from the right: a, d, g, q. Then up and down the right side; only how far that line goes changes (to the baseline for a, up to the top first for d, below the line for g and q).
2. A tall line, top to bottom: b, h, k, l.
3. A short line, from the middle down: i, m, n, r.

So b and d start differently: b with the line, d with the circle.

Schools teach different letter models, so compare these with the one your school uses.

The lowercase letter tracing worksheets are free: 26 printable pages, a to z, with a numbered dot where each stroke starts and an arrow for the way it goes. title: Free KDP cover template: bleed, spine and barcode box at 300 DPI
text:
A free KDP paperback cover template, sized to your book: pick the trim, the page count and the paper, and download one PNG at 300 DPI with every line on it.

Pink: the 0.125" bleed. It is trimmed off, so run background art to the outer edge.
Red line: the trim.
Blue dashes: keep text inside them, 0.125" in from the trim (KDP's rule) and from the spine folds.
Spine: text is allowed from 79 pages, kept 0.0625" in from each fold.
Grey box: the barcode area, 2" × 1.2", 0.25" in from the bottom and the spine. Amazon prints the barcode there, so keep it clear.

6×9, 120 pages, cream paper: 3765 × 2775 px.
The spine grows with the page count: 0.250" at 100 pages on cream, 1.000" at 400.

Put it in Canva, Photoshop or Affinity as the bottom layer, design over it, and hide it before you export the PDF. Every picture in the video is the template itself, drawn by the same code as the download button.

title: Free KDP interior templates: odd and even pages, gutter on the right side
text:
Free KDP interior page templates: one for odd pages and one for even pages, each a PNG at 300 DPI, exactly the size of the PDF page KDP expects for your trim, page count and bleed setting.

Why two: the gutter (the inside margin, against the spine) is on the left of odd pages (1, 3, 5…, the right-hand pages) and on the right of even ones. Putting it on the same side of every page is one of the mistakes that gets an interior rejected.

The gutter grows with the page count (KDP's table):
24 to 150 pages: 0.375"
151 to 300: 0.5"
301 to 500: 0.625"
501 to 700: 0.75"
701 to 828: 0.875"

With bleed, the page is 0.125" wider and 0.25" taller, so 6×9 becomes 6.125×9.25, or 1838 × 2775 px at 300 DPI. The extra goes on the outside edge, the top and the bottom only, never the gutter side.

Put the matching template under each page as the bottom layer, keep text inside the blue dashes, and hide it before you export. Every picture in the video is the template itself, drawn by the same code as the download buttons.

Free, no sign-up, made in your browser.

title: KDP printing cost: 24 pages and 110 pages are both $2.30 at 6x9
text:
On Amazon.com KDP charges one printing price for a black-ink 6x9 paperback from 24 to 110 pages: $2.30 (KDP help, "Paperback Printing Cost"). Past 110 it's $1.00 + $0.012 a page for the whole book: 112 pages $2.34, 150 pages $2.80.

Three real word search books, 15 words a puzzle, solutions in the back, page counts read from the rendered PDFs:
14 puzzles = 24 pages
88 puzzles = 110 pages
89 puzzles = 112 pages

So 88 puzzles is the most a 6x9 book holds for $2.30. Royalty at $8.99 is $2.20 at both 24 and 110 pages.
